title: Clinical education alone is sufficient to improve strength training exercise prescription
author: A/Prof Gavin Williams
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wsyfefw

steps.title: Recruit rehabilitation facilities
steps.instruction: Contact and obtain agreement from twelve neurological rehabilitation facilities (four public, four private, four rural) to participate in the education and training package study.

steps.title: Obtain ethics and consent
steps.instruction: Ensure every staff member who will provide research data signs the Patient Information and Consent Form (PICF); only physiotherapists or exercise physiologists are eligible for inclusion, while other staff may attend the workshop but not participate in data collection.

steps.title: Randomise facilities into clusters
steps.instruction: Perform cluster randomisation so that the four public facilities are randomised as a group, the four private facilities as a group, and the four rural facilities as a group, assigning six facilities to the intervention arm (ongoing mentoring) and six to the control arm (no mentoring).

steps.title: Baseline observation (pre‑education)
steps.instruction: An observer spends one full day in each facility before the workshop to record the number and type of gait‑related strengthening exercises prescribed to neurological clients, using the attached proforma.

steps.title: Deliver half‑day workshop
steps.instruction: Provide a half‑day workshop at each facility to all physiotherapy department staff, consisting of a lecture, case presentation, and practical demonstration on biomechanics of gait, gait disorders, and strength‑training exercises specific to walking.

substeps.instruction: Invite all physiotherapy department staff to attend.
Obtain informed consent from eligible staff before the workshop begins.

steps.title: Immediate post‑education data collection
steps.instruction: Immediately after the workshop, administer the knowledge questionnaire to consenting staff and record any immediate changes in exercise prescription (if observed).

steps.title: Implement ongoing mentoring (intervention only)
steps.instruction: For the six facilities randomised to the intervention, initiate a three‑month mentoring programme led by the lead investigator, including weekly team‑meeting issue raising, local case presentations, peer‑feedback, and booster support from a nominated local mentor.

steps.title: Three‑month follow‑up observation
steps.instruction: Three months after the workshop, an observer spends one full day in each facility to repeat the exercise‑prescription observation using the same proforma, and the questionnaire is administered again to assess knowledge retention.

steps.title: Data entry and management
steps.instruction: Code all hard‑copy questionnaire responses, enter them into a password‑protected electronic database, store hard copies in a locked filing cabinet, keep all participant information confidential, and destroy all data after five years in accordance with NHMRC guidelines.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Perform descriptive statistics on demographic data; use paired t‑tests to compare (i) time points 1 vs 2 for knowledge gain, (ii) time points 1 vs 3 for changes in exercise prescription, and (iii) time points 2 vs 3 for knowledge retention; use ANCOVA to determine whether ongoing mentoring is associated with greater change in exercise prescription.
